newsitem.title: USA: ABR says accounting analysis inaccurate.
newsitem.headline: ABR says accounting analysis inaccurate.

text.p: ABR Information Services Inc said Tuesday that a report disseminated by the Center for Financial Research and Analysis, focusing on the company's accounting treatment of interest income and software development costs, contained material inaccuracies.

With respect to interest income, $833,000 and $642,000 for fiscal years 1996 and 1995, respectively, were properly classified as revenue in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles, and not misclassified as the report states, ABR said.
This revenue, ABR said, constituted interest earned on customer account deposits, as specifically set forth in the notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements contained in its annual report.
Other interest income, in the amount of $3,014,000 and $573,000 in fiscal years 1996 and 1995, respectively, was also properly classified, ABR said.
ABR, as an information technology company, said it continues to develop and use software as it has reported in its public filings.
ABR's stock fell nine to 47 on Monday as momentum players sold the issue a few days after a top executive was removed, Reuters reported Monday.
